description: A pre-publish AI content checklist for product photos and video ads: match product details, add prices yourself, and follow platform rules. Save it now.
h1: An AI Content Checklist for Product Photos and Video Ads
lead: An AI content checklist is a last look at the product, the words, and the rights before a photo or a video goes on your store, a marketplace, or an ad account. AIVideosUGC can draft the script, match a presenter and a voice, lay captions on the spoken line, and you still run this check before anyone sees the file.
summary: Match the product, add prices yourself, license what appears, and follow the current labeling rule for each site you post on.

paras: What the generator makes, how to check a still and a clip, where the price goes, rights, labels, why shops use it, how to start in three steps, and how that compares with booking a shoot.

sections.h2: What Is an AI Video Ad Generator?
paras: It builds a short ad from your listing link, or from a couple of lines you type, then adds a script, a presenter, a voice, captions, and a cut you can trim, before the file goes on your store or into an ad account.

The checklist sits on top of that file. Check the product against what you ship, then the words, then the rights, then the rule for the site where it will appear. A generated photo or video is a new picture built from your upload, not a copy of the original file. A logo letter can shift, a button can move, a piece can appear, or a color can drift. The same pass works for a listing photo, a social post, and a paid ad.

sections.h2: See What to Review on a Finished Ad
paras: Watch the file the way a shopper will: on a phone, from the first frame, with the voice on and the captions in view. The pictures below are the kinds of stills and hand shots to hold next to the real item.

Filter the check by where it will run. A [TikTok ad](page:plat-tiktok) and a [Meta ad](page:plat-facebook) need the same product match, even when the frame is different. If you want more finished examples of the format, start from [AI UGC video ads](page:video-ads) and run this page's checks on the result.

sections.h2: How do I check AI product images?
paras: Hold the real item, or your original photo, next to the screen and go through color, shape, logos, parts, and size.

Compare color in daylight, not only on a bright monitor. Count pockets, straps, and buckles. Read every letter on a label. If a hand or a familiar object is in the frame, the product should look the right size beside it. A styled scene might add a candle or a plant. That is fine as decoration only if a shopper would not think it comes in the order. [AI lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos) are where those scenes are made, so review them with the same part count.

sections.h2: What is on an AI video review checklist?
paras: Play the clip on your phone, listen to the voice, read the captions, then step through it slowly, with extra attention on the hands and the first frame.

The script should name the product you ship, not a feature you do not sell. The presenter is a generated adult, not a customer who bought it. Movement is where a clip tends to slip: a label can blur as the product turns, fingers can blend into a strap, or a zipper can change shape halfway through. Count fingers and watch how they grip. The first frame often becomes the thumbnail. If one short moment is off, trim it in the built-in editor. If the problem runs through the clip, make a new version. Run this same check on an [AI product video generator](page:product-videos) clip before you post it.
sections.alt: Hands open the zipper and flap of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: Which checks should I do before I publish the price?
paras: Make the picture first, then add the price, the date, the code, and the headline yourself.

Do not ask for those words inside the image or the clip. Generated lettering is often garbled. Captions can follow the spoken line, and you still type the price, the date, and the code yourself so every character is the one on the product page. Before posting, match the price and the code to the store, and confirm any end date has not already passed. If stray letters appear on packaging or on a sign in the background, crop them out or try again.

sections.h2: What do I need to own before an AI ad goes live?
paras: Upload only photos you took or have the rights to use, and feature only logos that belong to you.

If you start from a supplier photo, your agreement with them needs to cover ads. Requests built around another company's marks, or around celebrities, may be refused. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded. For music, pick a track from the music library here, or a track you have already licensed for ads. The presenter and the voice you pick are there for the ads you make on AIVideosUGC.

sections.h2: When do AI-generated content labels apply?
paras: Read the current rule on each site you post to. Several platforms ask you to mark realistic generated people or scenes, and the rule changes.

Keep two rules on every site. Do not present a generated person as a real customer or reviewer, including in [AI model photos for clothing](page:model-photos). And do not let a caption promise health, skin, or weight results. Show how the product is used and let the shopper decide.

The meter is credits, not a day rate. A photo is 24 credits. A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second clip is 24, 40, 60, or 120. Starter is $24.50 for 200 credits a month, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Checked Video Ad
paras: A skincare shop has a presenter hold the bottle, say what is in it, and then someone checks the label against the real bottle.
A gadget shop opens the box on a desk and confirms every part in the kit is the part that ships.
A clothing shop shows the piece on an adult, then matches the neckline and the print to the sample.
A food shop sets the jar on a counter and has the voice name the flavor that is on the lid.
A candle shop lets hands lift the lid, and the caption follows that one motion.
A jewelry shop turns the piece once, and a person counts the stones before the file is posted.
A shop with buyers in two countries keeps the same presenter and speaks the script in the other language.
A two-person team makes the next hook from the photo they already checked, instead of booking another afternoon.
A marketplace seller pastes the listing link, then fixes any line that does not match the live product page.
A shop testing two openings keeps both clips, posts one, and holds the other until the first has run.
Build the ad from a link or a short prompt, with a script, a presenter, a voice, and captions. Then match the product, type the price yourself, and use only photos, logos, and music you can run.
Send it to TikTok or Meta, or download it with no watermark, only after that pass. If a buyer could feel misled, do not publish that file.

faq.q: What does an AI video ad generator make?
faq.a: A short ad from your listing link or from lines you type, with a script, a presenter, a voice, and captions. You still check the product, the words, and the rights before it runs.

faq.q: How do I create a video ad with AI?
faq.a: Paste your listing link or describe the item, review the draft script and the presenter, then download the frame you need or send it to TikTok or Meta.

faq.q: What should the finished ad include?
faq.a: A script about the product you ship, a presenter you are willing to label as generated, a voice, captions on the spoken line, and a frame the placement already accepts.

faq.q: What should I check before posting an AI-made video?
faq.a: Watch it on your phone from the first frame to the last. Confirm the product, the hands, the label, the voice, and the captions, then confirm any price you added matches the store.

faq.q: What if a prop looks like it comes with the order?
faq.a: Do not use that version, or say clearly in the listing what is included. Decoration is fine only when a shopper would not expect it in the box.

faq.q: Can I ask the tool to draw my discount code?
faq.a: No. Add the code, the price, and the date yourself after download so the characters stay correct. Captions can follow the spoken line, not the offer.

faq.q: Do I have to say a person is generated?
faq.a: Check the current rule for each platform or marketplace you use. Do not describe a generated person as a real customer, even where the site lets you mark the ad as generated.

faq.q: Can I use a supplier photo as the source?
faq.a: Only if your agreement with the supplier covers ads. Otherwise shoot your own photo.

faq.q: What if one moment in the clip looks wrong?
faq.a: Trim that moment in the editor if it is brief. If the error runs through the clip, make a new version instead of posting it.

faq.q: Can I publish the file to TikTok or Meta from here?
faq.a: Yes. After the checklist passes, send the file to TikTok or Meta, or download it with no watermark and upload it yourself.
